newsitem.title: NIGER: President's backers sweep Niger assembly polls.
newsitem.headline: President's backers sweep Niger assembly polls.

text.p: The political party supporting Niger's President Ibrahim Bare Mainassara swept an overwhelming majority of seats in legislative elections boycotted by the opposition, electoral officials said on Monday.

Official results of Saturday's election have yet to be announced but the officials told Reuters the Union of Independents for Democratic Renewal won 58 of parliament's 83 seats. A smaller party, the ANP, took eight seats while the rest were shared by a dozen or so minor parties and independents.
The Independent Elections Committee on Sunday put average voter turnout at only 27.32 percent, confirming the impact of a boycott by the main opposition parties opposed to Mainassara.
An alliance of eight main opposition parties demand a rerun of a chaotic July presidential election they say was rigged by Mainassara, who staged a coup as an army colonel last January.
The opposition hailed the success of the boycott.
Mainassara ousted the elected government of civilian president Mahamane Ousmane on January 27 following a long standoff between Ousmane and his prime minister.
He resigned from the army and offered himself as an independent candidate for elections in July.

But he suspended the electoral commission on the second day of polling, accusing it of irregularities, and placed his opponents under house arrest. He appointed a new commission which declared him winner with 52.22 percent of votes cast.
The United States said the election was fraudulent and suspended development aid.
